answer: A bridge market for saffron deliveries across a canyon locks one bond per simultaneous contract. Validators bind each bond to its contract ID and slash it for two conflicting signed results for that contract, not mere disagreement. One bond cannot back overlapping contracts; ten names seeking ten jobs must still lock ten bonds. Validators reject reused receipt IDs, then release bonds after a fixed dispute window. This prices concurrent commitments rather than counting keys as people. Wealthy attackers and false data lacking public proof remain risks.
